$comment: T-CYBER station configuration. Edit values here; the application re-reads this file automatically on the next page load. Recipient address changes reset that recipient to 'unverified' until a supervisor verifies it in Settings. All values below are synthetic demonstration data; use example.invalid addresses for demos.

station.name: PS Madhapur
station.address: Cyber Crime Wing, PS Madhapur, Madhapur, Hyderabad 500081 (synthetic)

delivery.$comment: How approved requests leave the station. "gmail" (prototype): they are sent from the Gmail account in "gmail" below, to the address the officer types. "via-io": each is mailed to the IO mailbox (ioMailbox) and the IO forwards it, then marks it as forwarded. "direct": sent straight to the nodal officer (needs the station mailbox's SMTP/IMAP access). transport applies to via-io: "simulated" keeps the mail in T-CYBER; "smtp" uses the mail server set in .env (SMTP_HOST, SMTP_PORT, SMTP_SECURE, SMTP_USER, SMTP_PASS).

gmail.$comment: Prototype link to one Gmail account. Every request draft is also kept in this account's Drafts; edits made in T-CYBER or in Gmail are carried to the other side; an approved request is sent from this account to the address the officer types. senderApproves: the officer who presses Send in the mail window approves the version they send (logged); set it to false to have another officer approve a version its author wrote. readReplies: replies that arrive in this account's inbox are read and linked to the request they answer (needs the read permission: connect again once after turning it on); mail that is not about a case is skipped and never stored. Put the Google OAuth client file (credentials.json) at credentialsFile, then run `npm run gmail:connect` once on this server and sign in to the account. Set enabled to false to switch the link off.
